I'm 65 years old and I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for 40 years. I have 10.1 mu total — 6 mu I do wheat-maize double cropping on, and the other 4.1 mu I plant cotton. My household has six people, but two of my sons work off-farm in Handan, so they send a bit of money back but they're not here for the busy season. That leaves me, my wife, and my daughter-in-law for most of the work. We hire a few days of help at wheat harvest and cotton picking, but I watch every yuan. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets and I talk to the extension fellow when he comes by the village. But to be honest, I mostly go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do. Last year my wheat got about 400 kg per mu, the maize was a bit lower because it turned dry in August and I only irrigated once, and the cotton gave me about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton. 

For the wheat this year, I'll plant my usual improved variety around October 10th. The extension guy says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've always done a bit more — I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer as base before planting, and then topdress with 20 kg of urea at jointing. That's about 17 kg N total. I know it's a little high, but I'd rather waste some fertilizer than risk a bad yield. I can't afford to lose a whole crop with my small farm. I'll irrigate four times: before winter freeze-up, at green-up in March, at jointing, and once at grain filling if it doesn't rain. Water costs money with the meters now — about 10 yuan each time per mu — but I need it. For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide once and keep an eye out for aphids.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest is always tight — sometimes only five or six days. I hire a custom planter because I don't have my own maize planter, and I plant hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble with almost no tillage. There's no time for deep plowing. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations if it doesn't rain — one at jointing and one at filling. I expect around 470 kg per mu if the weather is normal. My neighbor who has a bit more land gets about 500 kg, but his soil is better near the well.

For cotton, I plant in late April after spring plowing. Cotton needs a lot of hand labor for picking, so that's why I only keep 4.1 mu of it — my family can handle that much, but no more. I use an improved Bt variety. I spray less insecticide now than ten years ago because of the Bt, but I still watch for bollworm and aphids. I irrigate three times — at budding, flowering, and boll setting. That's the critical time. I'll get about 260 kg per mu if it's a normal year. 

I'm spending about 5,800 yuan on inputs this year. That's a lot for a smallholder like me, but wheat and maize prices have been steady and cotton gives us cash in the fall. I always keep a little reserve for emergencies — my wife's medicine, or if the pump breaks. I don't take risks I can't afford.
